pull.title: MINOR: Add streams group protocol integration test for warm-up tasks
pull.body:
This ports the scale-out warm-up scenario from
HighAvailabilityTaskAssignorIntegrationTest, which exercises the classic
protocol's client-side HighAvailabilityTaskAssignor, to the streams
group protocol. Under the streams group protocol, warm-up derivation
happens broker-side via an AssignmentRefiner, which defaults to a no-op
implementation, so the test enables the real AssignmentRefinerImpl
explicitly to get coverage of the actual warm-up behavior against a live
cluster with real KafkaStreams clients, which did not exist before.

The test proves the same property as the original: when a stateful app
scales out, the new instance is first handed a warm-up task rather than
being promoted to active immediately, and is only promoted once its
local state has caught up, at which point the promotion happens with
zero real state restoration because the warm-up's state is reused
directly.

Two mechanisms from the original test don't carry over and needed
replacements. There is no client-side assignment-listener equivalent
under the streams group protocol, since that callback is wired into the
classic protocol's client-side assignor, so warm-up assignment and later
promotion are instead detected by polling
KafkaStreams.metadataForLocalThreads() for a task moving from the
standby set into the active set. On the target-assignment side, the
streams group protocol currently only ships the sticky assignor, which
balances active task load across processes rather than doing plain round
robin, but its load-balancing quota math still forces one of the two
tasks in this scenario onto the new, empty instance's target assignment,
which is exactly the mismatch the refiner needs in order to stage a
warm-up. So the test works with the sticky assignor as is, and does not
need to wait for a more round-robin-like assignor.

The rack-aware parameterization from the original test was dropped,
since the streams group protocol's sticky assignor has no rack-aware
placement logic today, so that axis would not exercise anything
meaningful. The in-memory versus persistent store parameterization was
kept, since it is a pure client-side choice orthogonal to the group
protocol.

### Test plan

- Ran both parameterized variants locally against a live 3-broker
embedded KRaft cluster; both pass.
- Confirmed via logs that the new instance is assigned a warm-up task
before promotion (`warm-up tasks {0_1}`, no active task), and that the
state-restore listener reports zero restored records at promotion time.
- `./gradlew spotlessApply checkstyleMain checkstyleTest` is clean.

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>

review_comments.body: Promotion is asynchronous, so the second metadata read can legitimately observe this task as active immediately after `findStandbyTaskId` observed it as a standby. In that valid warm-up→promotion race, `NoRetryException` makes the test fail instead of accepting the warm-up observation. Remove this second read (the observed standby already establishes the intermediate state), or inspect both roles from one metadata snapshot.

Removed the second read. It was checking that the observed standby task isn't also active, but that check is tautologically true within a single `metadataForLocalThreads()` call (active/standby task registries are disjoint under the same thread lock), and reading it from two separate calls introduces exactly the promotion race you're describing. The standby observation alone is what proves the warm-up was staged.
what does this reference to `testing-only` mean?

if we don't have standby tasks enabled shouldn't this assert that `kafkaStreams0` doesnt' have this task at all?  I guess it's being validated but maybe make it more explicit? Maybe I'm being too picky but I'm getting at it shouldn't find the task at all so maybe rename to `findTask` or something like that
Should this method get called from `TestUtils.waitForCondition` to eliminate flakiness due to variances in how long it takes to release the task?

It refers to `GroupCoordinatorConfig.STREAMS_GROUP_ASSIGNMENT_REFINER_CLASS_CONFIG`'s own doc string, which literally says "This should be used for testing only" — it's a broker-internal config because warm-up derivation isn't wired in as a production default yet. Expanded the javadoc to say that explicitly instead of just the parenthetical.

Right, with no standbys configured (streams.num.standby.replicas defaults to 0) kafkaStreams0 should have no trace of the task at all, not just no longer be active. Added a hasTask helper that checks both active and standby sets and used it for this assertion instead.

Yes — checked StreamThread.setState, and threadMetadata is only recomputed when transitioning back into RUNNING, so the exposed snapshot can briefly still show the pre-revocation state while kafkaStreams0 is mid-transition. Wrapped it in waitForCondition.

I think this introduced a race condition: if the test code is slow, the warmup could become hot and get promoted to active before this condition runs (not sure if the heartbeat interval which is much larger is high enough to avoid the race -- we sometime have very slow CI runs...)

commit.message:
Add streams group protocol integration test for warm-up tasks

Ports the scale-out warm-up scenario from HighAvailabilityTaskAssignorIntegrationTest
(classic protocol) to the streams group protocol. The new test enables the real
AssignmentRefiner broker-side (NoOpAssignmentRefiner is the default) and proves that a
newly added instance is first handed a warm-up task, then promoted to active only once
caught up, reusing the warm-up's local state with zero real restoration. Since there is
no client-side assignment-listener equivalent under this protocol, warm-up and promotion
are detected by polling KafkaStreams.metadataForLocalThreads() instead. The sticky
assignor's per-process load balancing is enough to force the necessary task movement onto
the new instance for this scenario, so no rack-aware parameterization is needed here.

commit.message:
Remove racy standby-not-active check in warm-up test

metadataForLocalThreads() takes a fresh per-call snapshot, so checking that a
just-observed standby task isn't active via a second, separate call can race with
a legitimate promotion in between. The check was also tautological when done from
a single snapshot (a task can't be in both registries at once), so the standby
observation alone is sufficient to prove the warm-up was staged.

commit.message:
Address code-review findings on the streams group warm-up test

Reuse IntegrationTestUtils.produceSynchronously instead of a hand-rolled
producer loop, so a failed send surfaces as a clear error instead of being
silently swallowed. Assert kafkaStreams0 actually releases the task once
kafkaStreams1 is promoted, closing a split-brain coverage gap. Simplify the
restore-listener's AtomicLong bookkeeping to a plain set, since this test's
scale-out shape guarantees only one task is ever warmed up. Make that
guarantee explicit with an assertion in findStandbyTaskId instead of leaving
it an implicit assumption. Create the changelog topic with cleanup.policy
compact to match what Kafka Streams itself would provision. Cache the topic
end-offset sum once per poll iteration instead of recomputing it twice.

Address bbejeck's review: check full task release, poll for it, clarify javadoc

kafkaStreams0 should have no trace of the promoted task at all once released
(streams.num.standby.replicas defaults to 0), not just no longer be active, so
broaden the check to any role. Poll for it instead of checking once, since a
thread's exposed metadata snapshot only refreshes on transition back into

the class javadoc to explain what "testing-only" means for the refiner config.

issue.title: MINOR: Add streams group integration tests for the warm-up task lifecycle

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
This extends the end-to-end coverage of warm-up tasks under the streams
group protocol beyond the scale-out case in #23608, with real Kafka
Streams clients against the real AssignmentRefinerImpl. The tests cover
the warm-up budget when two members join at once (only one migration is
warmed up while the other waits, and the waiting one is warmed up rather
than moved cold once the budget frees), and the scale-in mirror of
#23608, where a member leaving makes the target assignment no longer
want an in-flight warm-up task, which is then given up while its owner
keeps running the task. Warm-up revocation was so far only verified at
the coordinator level. They also cover the client reporting a warm-up
task's offsets on the next heartbeat once it is caught up, even with a
task offset interval far longer than the test, promotion being gated on
acceptable.recovery.lag (withheld at a known lag above the threshold,
promoted once the threshold is raised while the lag is held constant),
and tasks moving cold with no warm-up task when num.warmup.replicas is
0.

Where a test has to hold a warm-up task behind, the instance's restore
consumer, which unlike the main consumer is still taken from the client
supplier under the streams group protocol, lets a small budget of
records through and then withholds the rest. A budget is needed rather
than a gate that is closed from the start, since a warm-up task that has
restored nothing reports no offset, and there would be no lag to gate
on. EmbeddedKafkaCluster gains setters for the warm-up related group
configs, and setGroupHeartbeatTimeout is renamed to
setGroupHeartbeatInterval, since it sets streams.heartbeat.interval.ms
and the old name suggested a timeout.

The tests surfaced that a client reports an active task's restore having
finished only with its next offset report, which can be up to
streams.task.offset.interval.ms later, and that until then the refiner
takes the owner to still be restoring and moves the task without warming
it up. The tests therefore run with the shortest task offset interval
and wait for the broker to see all active tasks running before staging a
migration.

Tests for coordinator failover, the active owner leaving mid-warm-up,
and members with several stream threads follow in a separate PR stacked
on this one.

The test class passed repeated local runs (20 consecutive runs before
the split, with one failure traced to a race in the test itself and
fixed). Each key assertion was also checked against a mutation that
should break it: disabling the client's hot warm-up report trigger,
making isCaughtUp ignore the threshold, and making the refiner ignore
the warm-up budget each make the corresponding test fail.

Reviewers: ChickenchickenLove <ojt90902@naver.com>, Bill Bejeck
 <bbejeck@apache.org>

issue.title: MINOR: Fix race in StreamsGroupWarmupTaskIntegrationTest

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
The test sampled the thread metadata for a standby task to detect the
warm-up. The metadata shows it only until the promotion, so a test
thread stalled for about two heartbeat intervals missed it and timed
out. Record the warm-up's start and its promotion through a
StandbyUpdateListener instead.

Follow up to https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23608

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
